newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian weather - grain belt still needs rain.
newsitem.headline: Australian weather - grain belt still needs rain.

text.p: Patchy weekend rainfall in Australia's eastern and southern states left growers still in need of significant rain to establish 1997/98 crops.

Reasonable rainfalls were recorded in southern parts of New South Wales but overall rainfall in Australia's eastern and southern grain growing areas did little to assist crops, producer bodies, grains traders and weather officials said.
Bureau of Meteorology forecasts are for little or no rain for the rest of the week.

Most growers said patchy weekend rain in South Australia (SA), Victoria and NSW was inadequate, although some had quite good rains in particular areas, Phil Lindsay of broker Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures said.

A forecasting official with the NSW branch of the Bureau of Meteorology said while reasonable weekend rain fell in parts of the state's wheat belt, fine weather was forecast for the week. The bureau's forecast remained for significantly drier than normal conditions across much of eastern Australia, including Queensland, Victoria, southern NSW and south Tasmania, he said.
An official with the Victorian branch of the Bureau of Meteorology said that slight rainfalls over the weekend were probably not enough to be useful for crops.
"It was enough to get the ground wet," he said.
Falls of about eight millimetres in main wheat growing areas in the state's northwest contrasted with falls of about 28 mm in the northeast, which produces only limited amounts of grain.
"Victoria will be pretty well fine the rest of the week."
The state's dairy farmers were presently hardest-hit through shortages of feed grain, he said.
A Bureau of Meteorology monthly report, to be issued Thursday, would show dry and cold weather with higher than average mean sea level temperatures reflecting an El Nino event.
Southern Oscillation Index figures, based on air pressure, would be shown to be still strongly negative, he said.
A SA weather official said while some rain fell in the state over the weekend, it was mainly concentrated around the southern coast and ranges with not much inland.
The upper north of the state, which has had a "dire shortage" of rain, received only two mm, he said. The rest of the week held not much prospect of rain.
"We're coming out of the period of the year when crops can continue to exist on very little moisture because of the overall low growth of this time of year ... a semi-dormant phase."
Falls of up to an inch of rain over the weekend would have been very favourable for areas which received them, he said.
Western Australian crops were progressing the best in the country, he said.

A private grains trader in Armidale in the NSW agricultural belt said patchy weekend rain of between two and 20 mm in scattered wheat growing areas was a "great help" for some growers, but results were mixed.
The state of Queensland also showed patchy weekend rain without many heavy falls, a state weather official said.
The outlook this week was for not much rain apart from isolated showers along the coast, he said.
A crop forecast official with the Australian Wheat Board said serious consequences were feared in SA if the weather pattern did not turn around soon, he said.
However, dryness in Australia's grainsbelt so far this year fortunately had been during the least growth-oriented phase of the wheat crop cycle, he said.
Crops were dying in western areas of NSW, with reports in some areas there that crops would not be harvested, he said.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
